detail.longDescription: I haven’t really used Amazon Web Services in over ten years, but I kept an instance there and get charged about five bucks a month for it. Now all I want to do is download my data and shut everything down, so I’m no longer charged for anything. The problem is that I barely understood AWS to begin with, and it’s become massively more complicated in the time since I last used it. So, I have one EC2 instance (currently stopped), and two EBS volumes (one 19 GiB, one 8 GiB). The EC2 instance is running Ubuntu. What’s the simplest (and, if there’s a cost involved, cheapest) way to download everything and shut it all down? This question is sort of like How to migrate all files from Amazon EC2 Instance to Hard Drive , only I don’t need to re-upload the data, I want the data to be readable on my computer once downloaded, and I want to shut everything down (on the AWS side) afterward. (Also, I can’t really follow the instructions in that question’s answers because they assume a level of sophistication with AWS that I, sadly, lack.) Oh, and while I may be an AWS novice, I know my way around the Linux command line enough to use things like SSH and SCP (with some help from the ol’ man pages), so if those are required I’ll use those. But, I don’t really want to play around and see what works because I don’t want to incur any unnecessary costs. Besides, I figure you people probably have better ideas of where to start than I do!
